cards.text: Friend, we made it to the very last chapter of Isaiah. The LORD has just promised comfort for Jerusalem and said His wrath will be shown to His enemies. Now the prophet says look: the LORD will come with fire, and His chariots are like a whirlwind.

cards.question: The LORD is coming with fire, His chariots like a whirlwind. What is He coming to do?

answers.text: Carry out His anger and rebuke
Rest in a house built for Him

cards.question: By fire and by His sword, the LORD will execute judgment on all ___.

cards.text: Many will be slain by the LORD. Then the LORD calls out a group: people who consecrate and purify themselves to enter the groves.
They follow one in the center of those who eat swine, vermin and rats. Getting all purified so you can go eat RATS is like washing your car right before you take it mud-riding.

cards.question: The LORD says the people who purify themselves to enter the groves will perish together.

cards.text: Now here comes the turn. The LORD says He knows their deeds and their thoughts, and He is coming to gather.

cards.question: Who is the LORD coming to gather?
The LORD says the gathered nations "will come and see My ___."

cards.text: The LORD says He will establish a sign among them and send survivors to the nations: Tarshish, Put, the archers of Lud, Tubal, Javan and the islands far away.
TARSHISH! That's where Jonah's ship was headed when he ran from the Lord (Jonah 1:3). This time the LORD is the one booking the trip.

cards.question: The islands far away have already heard of the LORD's fame and seen His glory.
The LORD sends survivors out to faraway nations. What will they do there?

cards.text: The survivors are out there telling the nations about the LORD's glory. Then the LORD says they will bring all your brothers from all the nations.
They come on horses, chariots, wagons, mules AND camels. That's every ride on the lot, and here I am getting around by hopping on a gold base.

cards.question: Where are all those brothers brought from the nations?

answers.text: To the top of Mount Sinai
To the top of Mount Carmel

cards.question: The brothers are brought from all the nations as a ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: The LORD says it's just like the Israelites bringing an offering in a clean vessel to His house. People carried in like a holy offering.

cards.question: The LORD says He will select some of those gathered as what?

cards.text: Picked up and handed a job you never saw coming? Friend, a worn-out stamper from the back of a junk drawer knows THAT feeling.
Then the LORD talks about the new heavens and the new earth, which He will make. They will endure before Him.

cards.question: Just as the new heavens and new earth will endure, the LORD says, "so your ___ and your ___ will endure."
The LORD says that from one New Moon to another and one Sabbath to another, only Israel will come to worship before Him.
As the worshipers go forth, what does the LORD say they will see?

answers.text: The corpses of those who rebelled
A river flowing from the mountain

cards.question: The LORD says the fire of the men who rebelled against Him will one day be quenched.

cards.text: Their worm will never die, and they will be a horror to all mankind. That's the last verse of Isaiah, friend: glory for every nation, and a sober warning to close the book.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 9 quotes "will come and see My ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 9 quotes "so your ___ and your ___ will endure.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card tells facts from the previous passage (the LORD promising comfort for Jerusalem and saying His wrath will be shown to His enemies, Isaiah 66:13-14) but gives no reference for them. The card cites only Isaiah 66:15.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: No story card sets up Isaiah 66:16. The blank asks the baker to guess the next word of the line ('judgment on all ___' with flesh, idols or islands). This tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The joke 'Getting all purified so you can go eat RATS' gives the group a reason the text doesn't give. Isaiah 66:17 says they consecrate and purify themselves to enter the groves, following one in the center of those who eat swine, vermin and rats. It never says they purify themselves in order to eat rats.

rule.text: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' ('Only the tribes of Israel', 'Only the priests and Levites'), and the right answer doesn't. This pattern lets the right answer stand out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The blank is the next word of a quoted line ('will come and see My ___'). The baker has to guess the exact wording (glory, temple or city) instead of reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 1 follow a strict rotation: multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, multiple choice.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers share the pattern 'To the top of Mount ...'. The right answer, 'To His holy mountain Jerusalem', is worded differently and sounds more like the Bible, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'People carried in like a holy offering' calls the offering holy. Isaiah 66:20 compares them to an offering brought 'in a clean vessel' and never calls it holy.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card tells no part of the passage. It is only a joke about the junk drawer. Isaiah 66:21 was already covered by card 6, so the card cites a verse it doesn't tell and doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This two-blank card asks the baker to guess the exact words of a quoted line ('so your ___ and your ___ will endure'). Nothing on the earlier cards lets the baker reason their way to descendants and name.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 'Glory for every nation' stretches the text. In Isaiah 66:18-19, the nations come and see the LORD's glory, and His glory is proclaimed among them. The text never says the nations receive glory.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
